advancedConcurrentMediaHelp: Use 0 for no limit, which is the default. Once the limit is reached a new live view is refused and a new still is answered with that camera’s most recent picture, and a camera already open is never interrupted. Lower this if several cameras at once make live view stutter.
advancedConcurrentMediaInvalid: Enter a whole number of cameras greater than or equal to zero.
advancedDeviceHelp: Exposure, audio, and snapshot preferences for one device open from that device’s tile.
advancedFfmpegHelp: Leave blank to use the FFmpeg executable bundled with the plugin.
advancedLiveVideoPassthroughHelp: Turn this on if live view never shows, or if the log says FFmpeg stopped before sending video. Live video from cameras that record H.264 is then sent as the camera recorded it, as version 4 did, instead of being converted to what the Home app asked for.
advancedHardwareVideoEncoderHelp: Use the computer’s video hardware: turn this off if live view stopped working after an update or looks wrong.
advancedHdLiveVideoHelp: Turn this on if live view in the Home app looks blurry. Cameras then offer the Home app only 720p and 1080p, also on mobile data and in the camera grid, which uses more data.
advancedIgnoreHomeBitRateHelp: Turn this on if live video looks sharp for a few seconds, then blurry or blocky. Video is then converted at a constant quality close to the camera’s own, instead of the low bit rate the Home app asks for, which uses more network bandwidth.
advancedIgnoreHomeBitRateLabel: Ignore the Home app’s bit rate limit
advancedPollingHelp: Use 0 to disable scheduled polling. The default is 10 minutes.
advancedPollingInvalid: Enter a whole number of minutes greater than or equal to zero.
advancedSmallVideoPacketsHelp: Turn this on if the Home app keeps loading a camera but never shows the live picture. Live video is then sent in smaller network packets, as version 4 did.
advancedSaveFailed: The advanced setting could not be saved. Try again.
advancedSummary: Change infrequent host-level options. Save the Homebridge configuration when finished.
advancedWarmUpHelp: Choose the events that should open a camera’s connection as soon as it reports one, so the live view or snapshot straight afterwards starts immediately. Every camera is independent: an event opens only the camera that reported it, and only for the events chosen here. A camera running on its own battery is kept awake for several minutes each time, and one reporting often may never sleep; wired cameras and those behind a HomeBase are unaffected. Doorbell presses alone is the balanced choice.
advancedWarmUpRemove: Stop warming up the selected events
armingModesHelp: Four HomeKit states, nine station modes. Pick what each state sets; leave one empty to keep it out of HomeKit. Night has no default.
attentionUnreachableSummary: Homebridge Eufy cannot reach this device, so HomeKit shows it as not responding. Check that it has power and a connection, then diagnose it if it stays unreachable.
authCommitFailed: Signed in, but the session could not be saved. Restart Homebridge and sign in again.
authFailed: Authentication failed. Check the account details and try again.
authPluginRunning: Homebridge Eufy is using the account connection right now. Restart Homebridge, then sign in again.
authSaveFailed: Signed in, but the settings could not be saved. Press Save.
authSuccess: Authentication succeeded. Press Save below, then let Homebridge restart to start the new account connection.
authSummary: This temporary connection stays in the setup window and closes before your account is saved.
authTimedOut: Authentication timed out. Start again to create a fresh connection.
cameraOwnArming: This camera also appears as its own security system. It works without a HomeBase, so it keeps its own arming state rather than following one — which is why each standalone camera shows a separate security system in the Home app.
captchaRetry: That answer was not accepted. Enter the new captcha.
countryInvalid: Enter a two-letter country code, such as US or FR.
dashboardAuthenticationRequiredSummary: The saved account needs authentication before devices can reconnect.
dashboardDegradedSummary: Showing the last complete discovery while the connection recovers.
dashboardDegradedTitle: Devices from the last complete discovery
dashboardFailedSummary: Homebridge Eufy stopped on an error. Restart Homebridge.
dashboardIncompleteSummary: Device discovery is incomplete. Existing device information is retained until a complete discovery replaces it.
dashboardMissingSummary: No device snapshot is available yet. Start or restart Homebridge to discover devices.
dashboardOwnerConflictSummary: Another Homebridge Eufy process owns this account connection. Stop the other process before continuing.
dashboardReadySummary: These devices came from the latest complete discovery.
dashboardRestartRequiredSummary: These devices were found for the account you just signed in to. Press Save below, then let Homebridge restart to connect them.
dashboardStaleSummary: The saved device snapshot is no longer current. Restart Homebridge to refresh its status.
dashboardUnreachableSummary: The settings service did not answer. Reload this page.
diagnosticDescription: This device is recognized, but its primary capabilities do not have a verified HomeKit representation yet.
diagnosticNoAction: Nothing is wrong with your setup and there is nothing here to fix. It will appear in HomeKit once its main function has a representation verified against real hardware, so reporting it only helps if you can assist with that.
diagnosticsArchiveHandoff: Your browser should have saved {filename}, usually in Downloads. On the GitHub issue, write when the problem happens, what you expected, and whether it happened during this capture. Drag the file into the Diagnostics Archive box without renaming it, and check that its name appears there before submitting.
diagnosticsCaptureKeepsRunning: You can close this page; the capture keeps running and stops on its own on {time}.
diagnosticsCaptureTimedOut: The capture stopped after 72 hours. Download what was captured.
diagnosticsCollectingFinishHere: Diagnostics — a capture is running. Finish it here.
diagnosticsControlAction: Use the control once, wait for the device to settle, then finish when the wrong state is visible.
diagnosticsControlSummary: Checks what happens when a HomeKit control and the device disagree.
diagnosticsDashboardAction: Repeat the navigation, setting change, or save attempt once, then reopen Diagnostics from the bug icon to finish the capture.
diagnosticsDashboardSummary: Tracks a problem in the dashboard, login, or setup screens.
diagnosticsDevicesAction: Refresh the devices or reopen the affected tile, then finish when the problem appears.
diagnosticsDevicesSummary: Checks why a HomeKit accessory is missing, duplicated, or shown as the wrong type.
diagnosticsExistingIssue: Attach it to my existing GitHub issue
diagnosticsFailed: The diagnostics request failed. Try again.
diagnosticsLiveAction: In the Home app, open the live view, request one snapshot, or try talkback once. If the image stays black or the problem shows, come back here and press finish. If it works, leave the capture running and try again when the problem returns.
diagnosticsLiveSummary: Checks one live view, snapshot, or talkback problem.
diagnosticsMissingEvidence: Some details could not be captured. You can still download the diagnostics file.
diagnosticsOtherAction: Try to make the problem happen and note what you see. Once it has happened, come back here and press finish; until then, leave the capture running.
diagnosticsOtherSummary: Captures details for a problem that does not fit another choice.
diagnosticsPrivacy: Reporting a problem needs a GitHub account. Nothing is uploaded: the diagnostics file is encrypted, stays on your computer until you attach it to a GitHub issue yourself, and never includes passwords, private account data, or camera media.
diagnosticsProfileLiveMedia: Black screen or live video problem
diagnosticsRecordingAction: Trigger one event that should be recorded and wait a few minutes. If the recording is missing or will not play, come back here and press finish. If it plays, leave the capture running and try again when the problem returns.
diagnosticsRecordingSummary: Checks one missing or unplayable HomeKit Secure Video recording.
diagnosticsStartupAction: Restart Homebridge or repeat the failed sign-in step, then return here and finish.
diagnosticsStartupSummary: Checks a Homebridge startup, connection, or sign-in problem.
firstSetupAcknowledgement: I have created a dedicated guest account and shared my Eufy home and devices with it.
firstSetupIntro: Create a separate Eufy account for Homebridge. From your personal account in the Eufy app, share your home and devices with that guest account.
firstSetupReasonBody: Your personal account stays active in the Eufy app on your phone. A separate account prevents the app and Homebridge from competing for the same session and interrupting either connection.
firstSetupTitle: Use a dedicated Eufy guest account
footnote: Independent and unofficial. Not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by Anker Innovations or eufy. "eufy" and "Anker" are trademarks of their respective owners. Use responsibly — rapid or failed logins can trigger captcha or temporary cooldowns.
legacySummary: These V4 settings were intentionally discarded. They were not migrated or executed.
log.action.allowBatteryCooling: Allow the device battery to return to a safe temperature.
log.action.checkCameraControl: Check the camera in the Eufy app; this control is unavailable until it reports its state.
log.action.checkCameraRecording: Check that HomeKit Secure Video is set up for this camera and that it reports motion.
log.action.checkCameraSnapshot: Check that the camera is reachable and can produce an image, then open the camera again.
log.action.checkFfmpegPath: FFmpeg could not be started; check the custom FFmpeg path in Advanced settings.
log.action.checkNetwork: Check network access and Eufy service availability.
log.action.checkPhysicalArmingMode: Check the physical security-system mode before retrying.
log.action.checkPhysicalLight: Check the physical smart-light state before retrying.
log.action.checkPhysicalLock: Check the physical lock state before retrying.
log.action.checkStation: Check that the station or HomeBase this camera uses is powered and online, and network access between Homebridge and it, then open live view again.
log.action.controlTimedOut: The device did not answer in time; use the Eufy app for this control, and attach a diagnostics file to your issue if it keeps happening.
log.action.enableCamera: Turn the camera on in the Eufy app, then open live view again.
log.action.mapArmingMode: Assign this mode to a HomeKit state under HomeKit guard modes in the device’s settings.
log.action.reduceConcurrentMedia: Open live view again; if it keeps happening, close a camera already open or raise Cameras streaming at once in Advanced settings.
log.action.retryCameraControl: Try the control again; the camera did not confirm the change.
log.action.retryLiveView: Open live view again, and check network access between Homebridge and the camera.
log.action.retryRecording: No action is needed; recording is attempted again on the next trigger.
log.action.retryTalkback: Close and reopen the camera, then try speaking again.
log.action.trySmallVideoPackets: If the live view never shows in the Home app, turn on Smaller live video packets in Advanced settings in the Homebridge Eufy dashboard.
log.action.setFfmpegPath: Set a custom FFmpeg path in Advanced settings.
log.homekit.armingReconciliationExpired: A security system did not confirm the requested mode
log.homekit.batteryTemperatureAlert: A device reported a battery temperature alert
log.homekit.cameraControlOperationFailed: A camera control did not take effect
log.homekit.cameraLiveSessionFailed: A live view ended without video
log.homekit.cameraLiveSessionRefused: Live view is unavailable because the camera is turned off
log.homekit.cameraMediaAtCapacity: Live view was refused because this host had reached its configured limit of cameras streaming at once
log.homekit.cameraRecordingFailed: A HomeKit Secure Video recording did not complete
log.homekit.cameraRecordingRefused: HomeKit Secure Video recording is unavailable because the camera is turned off
log.homekit.cameraRecordingUnavailable: HomeKit Secure Video recording is unavailable for this camera
log.homekit.cameraSnapshotUnavailable: A camera image is unavailable, so a placeholder is shown
log.homekit.invalidCameraControlObservat: A camera control state could not be read
log.homekit.invalidContactObservation: A contact sensor reading is invalid
log.homekit.lightReconciliationExpired: A smart-light did not confirm the requested state
log.homekit.lockReconciliationExpired: A lock did not confirm the requested target
log.homekit.unsupportedArmingMode: A security system reported a mode Apple Home cannot represent
log.homekit.unusableLockAnnouncement: A lock reported something this plugin cannot read, so its state is shown as unknown
oneAccountSession: One account session at a time
preferenceSaveFailed: The preference could not be saved. Try again.
reauthSummary: Homebridge Eufy can no longer use the saved Eufy session, so your devices are not updating in HomeKit. Sign in again to reconnect them.
sessionDetails: Sign-in, captcha, and verification will run here only after the plugin has stopped its existing Eufy connection. Your sign-in details stay within this setup flow.
shareLink: How to share your Eufy home
snapshotModeCloudDescription: Uses only a stored image without waking the camera.
snapshotModeHelp: Refresh suits most cameras and is the default. Choose Live if a picture is out of date and you would rather wait for a new one, or Cloud if waking this camera costs too much battery.
snapshotModeLiveDescription: Requests a fresh live image each time.
snapshotModeRefreshDescription: Returns the cached image immediately and refreshes it in the background at a limited rate.
twoFactorSent: Eufy has sent you a verification code. Enter it below.
updatePendingFailed: The restart could not be started. Restart Homebridge to use the installed version.
updatePendingManual: This page shows what the running version can do. Restart Homebridge to use the version you installed.
updatePendingSummary: This page shows what the running version can do. Restart to use the version you installed.
wizardRestartSummary: Restart Homebridge to connect your cameras. This assistant opens again on its own once the plugin is running, to go through each device with you.
wizardLiveStarting: Connecting to the camera. This can take up to 30 seconds.
wizardLiveFailed: The camera did not send video. Check it is on and online, then try again.
wizardEufySettings: Camera settings in the eufy app
wizardSettingSent: Sent. The camera confirms within a few minutes.
wizardSettingFailed: The camera did not take the change. Try again.
wizardHomeKitHelp: What the Home app shows of this device and how it behaves there. Saved with the plugin settings.
wizardEufyHelp: Sent to the camera itself, the same settings as in the eufy app.
wizardEncodersHelp: What turns your cameras' video into the stream the Home app plays. A hardware encoder is used only once it has passed a test when Homebridge starts; otherwise the processor codes the video.
wizardEncodersUnavailable: Could not read the encoder test. Try again.
wizardEncoderBytes: it made {coded} KB of video where {bound} KB fits the bit rate the Home app asks for
wizardEncoderFailed: it did not finish the test
wizardEncoderFormat: its video is not what the Home app asked for
wizardProbeRun: Test it again with other settings
wizardProbeRunning: Testing. This can take up to a minute.
wizardProbeNothing: Nothing to test: no encoder was turned down for size
